posts.text:
The U.S. hiring rate is still low at 3.3%
But it's off the *extreme* lows of 3.1% in February and 3.2% we saw in many months last year.

The "hiring recession" is over. 
It's now a winners & losers story in the labor market where some industries are improving, while others (esp. tech, finance) are bleak

posts.text:
Encouraging news: Job openings are at the highest level in 2 years.

May 2026: 7.6 million job openings
May 2025: 7.3 million job openings
May 2024: 7.8 million job openings

Industries with more job opening than a year ago:
+Most blue collar industries (manufacturing, construction, mining)
+Retail
+Professional and business services

Industries with fewer job openings than a year ago:
-Tech (information)
-Finance/insurance
-Healthcare
-Hospitality

posts.text:
Big news: The Supreme Court prevents President Trump from firing Fed Governor Lisa Cook.
This is a win for Fed independence. 
The vote was 5 to 4.

"The Founders knew from  experience the calamities that could arise from even the 'suspicion' of political manipulation of monetary policy."

Roberts, Sotomayor, Kagan, Kavanaugh and Jackson voted in favor of Fed independence. 

supremecourt.gov/opinions/25…

posts.text:
Americans are getting squeezed right now. They are no longer able to save much, if at all.

The personal savings rate has dipped to 3%
This is one of the lowest readings in the past 15 years.

Personal savings rate May 2025: 4.9%
Personal savings rate May 2026: 3%
There's been a downward trend for awhile, though it's been especially sharp for the past year.

JUST IN: Q1 GDP was revised up to 2.1%. 
But check out the reason...it happened due to far less imports than originally thought.

Consumer spending -- the backbone of the US economy -- was anemic in Q1. It should rebound in Q2, but it's worth watching closely.
posts.summary: GDP revised up but driven by import decline, weak consumer spending concerning

posts.text:
JUST IN: PCE Inflation jumped to 4.1% (y/y) in May -- That's the highest inflation in 3 years and it's due largely to the war in Iran impact.

Core PCE inflation (excluding food and energy) rose to 3.4% --> the highest since fall 2023. 

This is painful for the middle class and moderate income Americans.

The monthly gain (0.4%) was a bit softer than expected, but the key will be how fast does inflation cool this summer??

posts.text:
What a chart...
The labor market is getting worse for American moms.

Unemployment for college-educated moms of young kids keeps rising.
Employment-to-population ratio is way down

"Mom-cession" ?
Return to office is likely part of the story.
Expensive childcare another part of the story.
It's interesting to see the big drop off in college educated moms of young kids employed in healthcare/social assistance and education.

Important charts from @MattNestlerPhD

posts.text:
Gas prices are back below $4 for the first time since March 30.

The AAA average gas price fell to $3.999 today. 
That's still a dollar above where gas prices were before the war in Iran began. But it's a psychological milestone to see prices drop below $4 again

Warning: Getting back below $3.50 could be harder. In 2022, it took until after Thanksgiving to get back below $3.50
